newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Supersol denies Hungary unit being sold.
newsitem.headline: Supersol denies Hungary unit being sold.

text.p: Israel's Supersol Ltd denied a newspaper report on Monday that said it had started negotiations to sell its chain of supermarkets in Hungary.

"At the moment we are not looking for a buyer," Yehuda Freidenberg, deputy managing director for finance, told Reuters in response to a report in the financial daily Globes that it was in talks to sell the Super-Kozert chain.
Globes said Supersol was looking to sell the Hungarian stores because of their low profitability and estimated the value of the deal at $20-$25 million.
"We have in past been approached with requests to buy the stores from us, but we didn't sell," Freidenberg said, adding that the stores were at present breaking even.

Supersol, Israel's biggest food retailer, acquired the chain in 1994 from the Hungarian government and has expanded it to about 15 outlets. Super-Kozert marks the company's first and only foray outside its home base, although it has expanded into non-food retailing as well.
